questions.prompt: Why do task completions and long time logs go to a pending queue instead of paying out immediately?
questions.explanation: So the XP ledger is credible. A number nobody ever checks is a number nobody believes — and the point of tracking contribution is that it means something when a member cites it on an application.

answers.text: So the ledger stays credible enough to be worth citing
Because the system can't calculate the reward until an officer confirms it
To give officers a way to reward members they like
To spread XP grants evenly across the semester

questions.prompt: A member logged eight hours in one entry against a task that plainly took two. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Reject it with a reason. It's almost always a mistake — wrong task, or a week logged as one entry. Rejecting silently is how you teach someone to stop logging time at all, and then the club loses the data entirely.

answers.text: Reject it with a written reason so they can correct it
Reject it without comment to avoid an awkward conversation
Approve it — questioning members discourages participation
Leave it in the queue until they notice and withdraw it

questions.prompt: You want to halve the XP awarded for logging an hour. What's the right way to do it?
questions.explanation: Announce it, then change it. Members plan around these numbers, and a quiet reduction reads as a punishment even when it was a bookkeeping decision. Config changes are cheap; trust is not.

answers.text: Announce the change to the club first, then make it
Change it quietly — nobody tracks the exact numbers
Change it and retroactively adjust past grants to match
Ask each member to opt in to the new rate

questions.prompt: What actually governs what a member is permitted to do in Constellation?
questions.explanation: Role, plus per-project membership. Rank is recognition and grants no permissions at all — a Nestling officer can do everything a Celestial officer can.

answers.text: Their role and their project membership
Their rank on the XP ladder
How long they've been a member

questions.prompt: Leaving the pending reward queue unattended for a few weeks is harmless, since nothing is lost.
questions.explanation: False. Nothing is lost, but the feedback loop is. A member who finishes work in week one and sees the XP in week four learns that the system doesn't notice — which is the exact failure the reward system exists to prevent.
